findings.title: BasePaginator allows negative slice that crashes
findings.body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 computes start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset and then does queryset[start_offset:stop], so a prev cursor with negative offset is passed directly to Django. Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds with AssertionError (negative indexing is not supported), unlike Python lists, while sibling paginators raise BadPaginationError for offset<0. A client-supplied cursor like 0:-5:1 therefore causes an unhandled exception. Consequence: any authenticated user can trigger 500 errors on BasePaginator-based endpoints via crafted cursor (DoS).

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks datetime ordering
findings.body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw int cursor.value. When used with order_by='-datetime' as in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, the attribute is a datetime object so math.floor raises TypeError, and build_queryset compares a datetime column to an int instead of converting via datetime.fromtimestamp like DateTimePaginator does. Consequence: the optimized audit-log path crashes with 500 or filters incorrectly.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing crashes instead of paginating
findings.body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 enables queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start_offset when enable_advanced_features is true, claiming Django handles negative slicing and that it is safe because permissions are checked at queryset level. Django QuerySets reject negative slice bounds with AssertionError, unlike Python lists. A client-supplied cursor such as 0:-10:0 therefore raises an unhandled exception. Consequence: crafted cursor causes 500 errors (DoS) and the safety comment is false; other paginators correctly raise BadPaginationError for offset<0.

findings.title: Undocumented optimized pagination exposes broken paginator
findings.body: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:82 adds a client-controlled ?optimized_pagination=true switch that constructs OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime' and enable_advanced_features=True for superusers or members with global access. That paginator only supports numeric keys and explicitly enables negative-offset slicing, neither of which works for datetime-ordered audit logs. Consequence: privileged callers can trigger 500s and get inconsistent pagination behavior versus the default DateTimePaginator via an undocumented param.

findings.title: Misleading comment endorses negative offsets without validation
findings.body: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:28 adds a comment saying negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination, but Cursor.__init__/from_string still accepts any int offset with no validation, while OffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator and others reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError and BasePaginator/OptimizedCursorPaginator crash on negatives. Consequence: developers are misled to pass negative cursors expecting support, leading to 500 errors.
